mainTopic: Preparing food on יום טוב when part of it is for a גוי, for גבוה, or for animals: shared animals, shared dough, dog dough, and bread for soldiers
overview: This amud first finishes a ברייתא about sprinkling blood when the meat cannot be eaten that day. Its wording suggests this is allowed only after the fact. That challenges רבה בר רב הונא, and the גמרא answers that rabbinic rules for שבת are stricter than for יום טוב. Next, רב אויא סבא asks רב הונא whether one may slaughter on יום טוב an animal half owned by a גוי. רב הונא permits it and dodges the comparison to נדרים ונדבות. The גמרא then explains the difference: you cannot get a כזית of meat without slaughtering the whole animal, but offerings come 'from the table of the Most High.' רב חסדא adds that shared dough may not be baked, because it can be split during kneading. A משנה about dog dough challenges him, and the גמרא ends up saying a carcass is already on hand for the dogs, since רב חסדא rejects הואיל. Finally, רב הונא allows baking for soldiers if a child may eat the bread. A story about שמעון התימני challenges this, and the answer leads into a dispute of תנאים about cooking for animals on יום טוב, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: the offering is accepted so the parts can be burned at night
steps.stepSummary: The quoted ברייתא ends: the offering is accepted so that its אימורין can be burned in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The offering] is accepted, on condition that the sacrificial parts are burned at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting earlier. The ברייתא says the blood-sprinkling counts, so the altar parts (אימורין) can be burned that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is one where the meat cannot be eaten that day. Sprinkling the blood still has a purpose, because it lets the אימורין go on the altar in the evening. The next step will read the exact wording of this ברייתא closely.

keyTerms.meaning: It was accepted (the offering achieved acceptance)
On condition that / for the purpose of
The parts of a sacrifice that are burned on the altar

phrases.english: It is accepted,
phrases.notes: Continuation of a ברייתא begun on the previous amud.

phrases.english: on condition that he burn the sacrificial parts in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּרְצָה, עַל מְנָת לְהַקְטִיר אֵימוּרִין לָעֶרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a source quoted at the end of the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling the blood makes the offering accepted, so the אימורין may be burned at night.

steps.title: Reading the wording: only after the fact, not from the start
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'if he sprinkled' implies the act is allowed only after the fact (דיעבד), not from the start (לכתחלה).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he sprinkled' — after the fact, yes; from the outset, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא's wording. 'If he sprinkled' sounds like the act is accepted only once it is done, not something you should plan to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'if he did it' describes something already done. It does not tell you to do it. So the ברייתא seems to hold that sprinkling here is allowed only בדיעבד, and this inference sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He sprinkled (the blood on the altar)
From the outset, as a plan

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'אם זרק' as permission to sprinkle. The גמרא reads 'if he did' as a clue that one should not do it in the first place.

phrases.english: If he sprinkled,
after the fact — yes,
from the outset — no!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם זָרַק, דִּיעֲבַד — אִין, לְכַתְּחִלָּה — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a legal inference from the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: That sprinkling in this case is permitted only after the fact.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'אם זרק' in the ברייתא.

steps.title: This fits רבא but is difficult for רבה בר רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The inference supports רבא but contradicts רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רבא it works well. But according to רבה בר רב הונא, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the inference to challenge רבה בר רב הונא. He permitted sprinkling from the outset, while the ברייתא implies it is allowed only after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's view matches the ברייתא: only after the fact. רבה בר רב הונא allowed sprinkling לכתחלה, which clashes with what the ברייתא's wording implies.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (sets up a contrast)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rava it works out well,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא קַשְׁיָא!
phrases.english: but according to Rabba bar Rav Huna it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרָבָא נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the inference as a challenge against one of the two אמוראים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's ruling that sprinkling is permitted from the outset.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies the act is allowed only after the fact, which contradicts permitting it from the outset.

steps.title: The גמרא admits it is a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concedes that the challenge to רבה בר רב הונא stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is indeed difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא openly admits it has no full answer here, and the challenge stays standing. It will offer a possible way out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A one-word 'קשיא' as a reply is weaker than 'תיובתא' (a full refutation). It means the question is strong, but the opinion has not been thrown out entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: A full refutation (stronger than קשיא; mentioned here for contrast)

phrases.english: It is difficult.
phrases.notes: A concession, not a new question.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes the challenge raised in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge against רבה בר רב הונא is acknowledged as a real difficulty.

steps.title: Rabbinic rules for שבת are stricter than for יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: Possibly the ברייתא is about שבת, where rabbinic rules are stricter, while רבה בר רב הונא spoke about יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: a rabbinic prohibition of שבת is different from a rabbinic prohibition of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way to save רבה בר רב הונא. The ברייתא deals with שבת, but his ruling was about יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis were stricter with שבות on שבת than on יום טוב. So 'only after the fact' on שבת does not prove anything about יום טוב, where רבה בר רב הונא could still permit sprinkling from the outset.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge to רבה בר רב הונא can be answered by separating שבת from יום טוב, because the rabbis were stricter about שבת.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
a rabbinic decree of Shabbat is different
from a rabbinic decree of a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: שָׁאנֵי שְׁבוּת שַׁבָּת מִשְּׁבוּת יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second option after conceding the difficulty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'only after the fact' applies equally to יום טוב, contradicting רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about שבת, where rabbinic rules are stricter. On יום טוב, sprinkling from the outset may still be permitted.

steps.title: רב אויא סבא asks about slaughtering a half-גוי-owned animal on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא סבא asks רב הונא whether one may slaughter on יום טוב an animal owned half by a גוי and half by a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא סבא asked רב הונא: an animal that is half a non-Jew's and half a Jew's — may one slaughter it on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב אויא סבא asks whether you may slaughter on יום טוב an animal owned jointly with a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, cooking and slaughtering are permitted only for Jewish food (לכם), not for a גוי. Since half the animal belongs to a גוי, part of the slaughter seems to be for him, and that is the doubt.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִנֵּיהּ רַב אַוְיָא סָבָא מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Avya the Elder asked of Rav Huna:
An animal, half of which belongs to a gentile
and half of which belongs to a Jew,
what is the law regarding slaughtering it on a Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִנֵּיהּ רַב אַוְיָא סָבָא מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about what may be slaughtered on יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether partial ownership by a גוי forbids slaughtering the animal on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב הונא: it is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that slaughtering the jointly owned animal is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers briefly that you may slaughter the animal. He gives no reason here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he gives no reason, the ruling is open to a challenge. That challenge comes in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted to slaughter the animal on יום טוב.

steps.title: Challenge: how is this different from נדרים ונדבות?
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא challenges רב הונא: נדרים ונדבות are also partly for someone else, yet they may not be slaughtered on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: and what is the difference between this and vow-offerings and gift-offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא challenges the ruling by comparing it to נדרים ונדבות. Those are voluntary offerings that may not be slaughtered on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a נדר or נדבה, part goes on the altar (for גבוה) and part is eaten by people. That looks like a shared animal, so if a shared animal is permitted, why are these forbidden?

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference between

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה לִנְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת?
phrases.english: And what is the difference between this and vow-offerings and gift-offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה לִנְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 7 with a parallel case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's permission to slaughter a jointly owned animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נדרים ונדבות are also divided (altar and people), yet they are forbidden on יום טוב. The two cases should be treated the same.

steps.title: רב הונא deflects: a raven is flying!
steps.stepSummary: Instead of answering, רב הונא distracts his questioner by pointing to a raven in the sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: a raven is flying!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא does not answer the challenge. He changes the subject on purpose by pointing out a flying raven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a real rejection of the question, only a way to avoid it for now. The real answer comes later in the גמרא (steps 13–14).
steps.confusionAlert: 'A raven flies' is not a hidden legal hint. It is simply a distraction, as the next steps make clear.

phrases.english: He said to him: A raven is flying!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עוֹרְבָא פָּרַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Avoids answering the challenge of step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Not a real rejection, only a deflection of the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: None. רב הונא does not answer here; the גמרא supplies the answer in steps 13–14.

steps.title: רבה asks his father why he brushed off a great man
steps.stepSummary: רבה, son of רב הונא, asks why he dodged רב אויא, whom he himself had praised as a great man.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he left, רבה his son said to him: isn't this רב אויא סבא, whom the master would praise to us as a great man?
steps.whatsHappening: After רב אויא leaves, רב הונא's son questions how his father acted. He reminds him that he himself had praised רב אויא as a great scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son finds it odd to brush off someone his father respected. This sets up רב הונא's explanation in the next step.

phrases.english: When he left,
Rabba his son said to him:
Isn't this Rav Avya the Elder
whom Master would praise to us
that he is a great man?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נְפַק אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the deflection of step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב הונא avoided answering a respected scholar.

steps.title: רב הונא explains: I was exhausted, and the question needed real thought
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says he was worn out that day, and the question needed careful reasoning he could not give on the spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: what could I do for him? Today I am 'sustain me with cakes, comfort me with apples' (I am exhausted), and he asked me something that needs a reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself by quoting a פסוק from שיר השירים to describe how tired he was. He adds that the question needed a thought-out reason, which he could not give right then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the question was a good one, not a silly one. Its answer was not obvious, so the גמרא will now supply the missing reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Sustain me with cakes (a verse expressing exhaustion)

phrases.english: He said to him: And what should I have done for him?
I am today in a state of
"Let me lean against the stout trunks; let me couch among the apple trees,"
phrases.notes: Song of Songs 2:5. רב הונא means he was worn out from his public duties.

phrases.english: and he asked me about a matter
that requires reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וּמָה אֶעֱבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the son's question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was too exhausted to work out the reasoning the question needed.

steps.title: So what is the reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning that tells the shared animal apart from נדרים ונדבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the explanation רב הונא did not give. This line sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question goes back to רב אויא's challenge in step 8. Why is a jointly owned animal permitted, while נדרים ונדבות are forbidden?

phrases.english: And what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story to the halachic challenge raised in step 8, which steps 13–14 answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logical difference between a jointly owned animal and נדרים ונדבות.

steps.title: A shared animal is permitted: you cannot get a כזית of meat without slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering the shared animal is permitted, because even a small amount of meat needs a full slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal half a non-Jew's and half a Jew's may be slaughtered on יום טוב, because it is impossible to get an olive's worth of meat without slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב הונא's ruling. The Jew cannot get even a little meat without slaughtering the whole animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a כזית of the Jew's meat needs a full שחיטה, so the act is fully needed for Jewish food. The fact that the גוי also benefits does not turn it into slaughter for the גוי.

phrases.english: An animal, half of which belongs to a gentile
and half to a Jew
may be slaughtered on a Festival,
since it is impossible to obtain an olive-bulk of meat
without slaughtering.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵמָה חֶצְיָהּ שֶׁל גּוֹי וְחֶצְיָהּ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּתָּר לְשׇׁחְטָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the answer to step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The slaughter is entirely needed for the Jew's meat, so the גוי's share does not forbid it.

steps.title: נדרים ונדבות are forbidden: everything comes from the table of the Most High
steps.stepSummary: נדרים ונדבות may not be slaughtered on יום טוב, because whoever eats them receives their share from גבוה. So the whole animal counts as slaughtered for גבוה, not for people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But vow-offerings and gift-offerings may not be slaughtered on יום טוב, because when the כהנים receive [their share], they receive it from the table of the Most High.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why נדרים ונדבות are different. The whole animal belongs to גבוה, and the people who eat it are guests at ה׳'s table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the shared animal, the Jew truly owns his half, so the slaughter is for him. With an offering, no person owns a share; the כהנים are given their portion by גבוה. So the slaughter is entirely for גבוה, and slaughtering for גבוה is not permitted on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The table of the Most High (ה׳)

steps.whatToRemember: A jointly owned animal may be slaughtered on יום טוב, because the Jew needs the whole slaughter for his own meat. נדרים ונדבות may not, because everyone who eats them receives it from גבוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a key principle for sacrifices. People who eat קדשים do not own a share; they eat as guests of גבוה. This explains the difference between a partner's ownership and a sacrifice.

phrases.english: However, vow-offerings and gift-offerings
may not be slaughtered on a Festival,
since the priests, when they receive [their portions] —
they receive them from the table of the Most High.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל נְדָרִים וּנְדָבוֹת אָסוּר לְשׇׁחְטָן בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer and resolves רב אויא's challenge from step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two cases differ. A partner truly owns part of the animal, but those who eat a sacrifice receive it from גבוה, so slaughtering an offering is slaughter for גבוה and is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב חסדא: An animal half-owned by a גוי may be slaughtered on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that an animal owned half by a גוי and half by a Jew may be slaughtered on יום טוב, because even a כזית of meat needs a full שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: An animal that is half owned by a non-Jew and half by a Jew may be slaughtered on יום טוב, because it is impossible to get even an olive's worth of meat without slaughtering the whole animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new ruling. A partly-gentile animal may be slaughtered on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב you may only do מלאכה for food for Jews, not for a גוי. The problem is that half of this animal is the גוי's. But the Jew cannot get his own share of meat without slaughtering the whole animal. So the שחיטה counts as done for the Jew, and it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal (here, a kosher animal fit for slaughter)
An olive's volume, the minimum amount that counts as 'eating'

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
An animal, half of which belongs to a gentile
and half of which belongs to a Jew —
it is permitted to slaughter it on Yom Tov,
because it is impossible to get an olive-size of meat
phrases.notes: Even the Jew's own small share requires slaughtering the whole animal.

phrases.english: without a slaughtering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב חסדא restates the same ruling and reasoning from step 13 about an animal half-owned by a גוי. He does this to set up a contrast with jointly owned dough in the next step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A half-gentile animal may be slaughtered on יום טוב because the Jew's portion cannot be obtained without slaughtering the whole animal.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Dough half-owned by a גוי may not be baked on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: In the same statement, רב חסדא rules that dough half-owned by a גוי may not be baked on יום טוב, because it can be split during kneading.
steps.simpleTranslation: But dough that is half a non-Jew's and half a Jew's may not be baked on יום טוב, since he can divide it while kneading.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא continues his statement with a contrasting case. Shared dough is forbidden to bake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike an animal, dough can easily be divided. The Jew can take his half out during לישה and bake only that half. Since splitting is possible, baking the גוי's half would be baking for a non-Jew, which is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Both cases are owned 50/50. The difference is not the ownership. It is whether the item can be divided before the מלאכה is done.

phrases.english: Dough, half of which belongs to a gentile
and half to a Jew —
it is forbidden to bake it on Yom Tov,
because it is possible for him
to divide it during the kneading.

steps.triggerLanguage: עִיסָּה חֶצְיָהּ שֶׁל גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רב חסדא's statement, contrasting dough with the animal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shared dough may not be baked on יום טוב, because it can be divided and only the Jew's half baked.

steps.title: רב חנא בר חנילאי cites the law of dog dough
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר חנילאי raises an objection by quoting a source. Dough made for dogs, if shepherds also eat it, is treated like regular bread, and it may even be baked on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר חנילאי objected: Dough made for dogs, when shepherds also eat from it, requires חלה, may be used for an עירוב and a שיתוף, gets a ברכה and a זימון, may be baked on יום טוב, and can be used for מצה on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to challenge רב חסדא. This step quotes the source. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key line is 'ונאפת ביום טוב': this dough may be baked on יום טוב. But part of it will go to dogs, not people. This looks like the shared dough case, which רב חסדא forbade.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (usually from a תנאי source)
The portion of dough given to a כהן
May be used to make an עירוב
Make a זימון (group invitation to בירכת המזון)

phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Chanilai raised an objection:
Dough for dogs,
when the shepherds eat from it —
is obligated in challah,
and one may make an eruv with it,
and one may make a shituf (alley-merging) with it,
and one recites a blessing on it,
and one makes a zimun over it,
and it may be baked on Yom Tov,
phrases.notes: This is the line that matters for the challenge.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: and a person fulfills his obligation (of matzah) with it on Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב חָנָא בַּר חֲנִילַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה (חלה 1:8) that seems to contradict רב חסדא's ban on baking shared dough.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that dough which can be divided may not be baked on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dog dough is partly for dogs, yet the משנה lets you bake all of it on יום טוב.

steps.title: Why not split the dog dough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the challenge. Why may dog dough be baked? He could split it while kneading, just like in רב חסדא's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Couldn't he divide it during the kneading?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the attack directly. Dog dough looks just like the shared dough that רב חסדא forbade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב חסדא's logic, the human portion could be separated during kneading, so baking the dogs' portion should be forbidden. Yet the משנה allows baking the whole thing. So either the משנה or רב חסדא's reasoning seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And why? (questioning the reason for a ruling)
But isn't it so that... (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: But why (may it be baked)?
Isn't it possible for him to divide it during the kneading!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? וְהָא אֶפְשָׁר לֵיהּ לְמִפְלְגַהּ בְּלֵישָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out exactly how the ברייתא in step 17 contradicts רב חסדא in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's reasoning that dough which can be divided may not be baked for the non-permitted share.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dog dough can be divided during kneading just as easily, yet it may be baked whole.

steps.title: Dog dough is different: the dogs may get a carcass instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that dog dough is different. Since (הואיל) the dogs could be satisfied with a נבלה, all of the dough may end up eaten by people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Dog dough is different, because it is possible to satisfy the dogs with a dead animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא by showing why dog dough is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal of his might die, and he would feed the carcass to the dogs. Then the shepherds would eat all the bread. Since every part of the dough could become human food, baking all of it counts as baking for people. This reasoning is called הואיל ('since it is possible').

keyTerms.meaning: Since (it is possible that...); judging a case by what could happen, not only by what is planned now
An animal carcass not slaughtered properly

phrases.english: Dog dough is different,
since it is possible to appease them with a carcass.
phrases.notes: Then the whole dough could go to the people.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי עִיסַּת כְּלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18 by setting dog dough apart from ordinary shared dough.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (שאני): the cases differ because of a possibility (הואיל).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dog dough is just like shared dough, since both can be divided.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dog dough is an exception. Since the dogs could eat a carcass instead, all of it may become human food, so baking it all is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer relies on הואיל. That opens the next question: does רב חסדא even accept הואיל?

steps.title: Does רב חסדא even accept the principle of 'since'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. Elsewhere רב חסדא says that one who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday gets מלקות, against רבה, who says he does not. That suggests רב חסדא rejects הואיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב חסדא hold of 'since'? But it was stated: one who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday — רב חסדא said he is flogged; רבה said he is not flogged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 19 by asking whether רב חסדא accepts הואיל at all. It sets up a contradiction from another dispute, which the גמרא will explain next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 19 depends on הואיל. But in the case of baking on יום טוב for a weekday, רבה exempts the baker, and the reason (explained right later) is a הואיל argument. רב חסדא says he is flogged, so he seems to reject הואיל. Then he could not rely on it for dog dough.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he hold of...? (challenging whether a sage accepts a principle)
It was stated (introduces an אמוראי dispute)
One who bakes on יום טוב for a weekday

steps.confusionAlert: This step only quotes the מחלוקת. The גמרא explains why it depends on הואיל in the next step (step 21), and gives a new answer for רב חסדא in step 22.

phrases.english: And does Rav Chisda hold of 'since'?
But wasn't it stated:
One who bakes on Yom Tov for a weekday —
Rav Chisda said: He is flogged;
Rabba said: He is not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַב חִסְדָּא הוֹאִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 19 by arguing that רב חסדא does not accept the principle it relies on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that dog dough is allowed because of הואיל, offered in defense of רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the baking-for-a-weekday dispute, רב חסדא gives מלקות, which seems to reject הואיל. So הואיל cannot be used to defend his view.

steps.title: רב חסדא and רבה explain their opinions on baking for a weekday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the reasoning behind the מחלוקת quoted in the previous step. רב חסדא gives מלקות because he does not say הואיל. רבה gives no מלקות because he does say הואיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: He gets lashes. We do not say, 'Since guests might arrive and the bread would be fit for him, it counts as fit for him now too.' רבה said: He does not get lashes, because we do say 'since' (הואיל).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב חסדא and רבה disagree about baking on יום טוב for a weekday. This finishes the challenge from step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה reasons this way: guests could show up today, so the bread could be used on יום טוב. Because of that 'since,' the baking is not a full איסור and there is no מלקות. רב חסדא rejects this 'since' logic. So the answer in step 19, which relied on הואיל, cannot be used to defend רב חסדא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the מחלוקת between רבה and רב חסדא about הואיל, a principle used in many places in שס.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: He is flogged,
we do not say: 'Since, if guests happen to come to him,'
it is fit for him —
now too it is fit for him.'
Rabba said: He is not flogged,
we do say 'since.'
phrases.notes: Implied conclusion: רב חסדא cannot rely on הואיל.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: לוֹקֶה, לָא אָמְרִינַן הוֹאִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning of the מחלוקת cited in step 20, which completes that challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 19, which used הואיל to explain why dog dough may be baked.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא himself rejects הואיל, so an answer built on הואיל cannot defend his ruling.

steps.title: New answer: the shepherds already have a carcass for the dogs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא withdraws the הואיל answer. The dog-dough case is one where a נבלה is already available, so it is certain the dogs can be fed with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, do not say 'since it is possible.' Instead, the case is where he has a carcass on hand, so it is definitely possible to satisfy the dogs with the carcass.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces its earlier answer with a new one that does not depend on הואיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old answer said the dogs might be fed with a carcass that might become available. That is a 'maybe,' which is just הואיל. The new answer says a carcass is already there. So the shepherds will most likely eat all the dough themselves. This is real fact, not a hypothetical, so רב חסדא agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal carcass not slaughtered properly
To appease them (to satisfy the dogs)

steps.whatToRemember: The dog dough may be baked on יום טוב only because a carcass is already available for the dogs. So the dough is certainly for people. No הואיל is needed, and רב חסדא's ruling stands.
steps.confusionAlert: The difference between the old answer and the new one is 'possible' versus 'certain.' The old answer was a hypothetical (הואיל). The new one is an actual fact.

phrases.english: Rather: do not say 'since it is possible,'
rather, for example where he has a carcass,
so that it is certainly possible to appease them with the carcass.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לָא תֵּימָא הוֹאִיל וְאֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Withdraws the answer that was knocked down in steps 20 and 21, and gives a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): a carcass is already on hand.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dog dough was allowed only because a carcass might become available (הואיל).
steps.terutzMaskana: A carcass is actually available, so the dough is certainly for people. This fits רב חסדא without using הואיל.

steps.title: Question to רב הונא: may villagers bake on יום טוב for the soldiers' quota?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא is asked whether Jewish villagers may bake bread on יום טוב when the authorities forced them to supply flour or bread to gentile troops.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב הונא: These village residents had the obligation to supply flour for the soldiers placed on them. May they bake it on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. Someone asks רב הונא a practical question about baking on יום טוב for gentile soldiers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread is made for non-Jews, and cooking on יום טוב is allowed only for Jews (לכם). The question is whether this bread could still count as fit for Jews in some way.

phrases.english: They asked Rav Huna:
These residents of a village
upon whom were imposed flour for the soldiers,
what is the law about baking it on a Festival?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִנֵּיהּ מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case on the same theme: baking on יום טוב when the food is mostly for others.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether baking on יום טוב is allowed for bread that must be given to gentile soldiers.

steps.title: רב הונא: it depends on whether a child may eat from it
steps.stepSummary: If the soldiers do not mind when a loaf is given to a child, every loaf is fit for a Jew, so baking is allowed. If they do mind, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: We check. If they give bread to a child and the soldiers are not strict about it, then each and every loaf is fit for a child, and it is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question with a test: does every loaf have a real chance of being eaten by a Jew?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the soldiers let a child take bread, each loaf could end up with a Jewish child. So baking each loaf counts as baking food fit for Jews. If the soldiers are strict, the bread is only for gentiles, and baking it on יום טוב is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They are strict and mind it

phrases.english: He said (to him): We examine:
if they give bread to a child
and they are not particular,
each and every one is fit for a child,
and it is permitted.
And if not — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזֵינָא אִי יָהֲבִי לֵיהּ רִפְתָּא לְיָנוֹקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Baking is permitted only if the soldiers do not mind a child eating from the bread, which makes every loaf fit for a Jew.

steps.title: Challenge begins: the story of שמעון התימני and the raiding soldiers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב הונא. שמעון התימני missed the study hall on יום טוב night because soldiers came to his town, and the townspeople slaughtered a calf to feed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: There was a story with שמעון התימני, who did not come to the study hall last night. In the morning רבי יהודה בן בבא found him and asked: Why did you not come to the study hall last night? He answered: A raiding military unit came to our city and wanted to plunder the whole city. We slaughtered a calf for them, fed them, and sent them away in peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב הונא's lenient ruling by starting to quote a story. The ruling comes in step 26, and the challenge itself in step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story also involves cooking on יום טוב for gentile soldiers. The way the story continues will show that this was viewed negatively. That would seem to contradict רב הונא, who allowed baking for soldiers in some cases.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge)
A raiding or searching military troop

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
There was an incident with Shimon the Timnite
who did not come last night to the study hall.
In the morning Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava found him,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא בָּאתָ
phrases.english: he said to him: Why did you not come
last night to the study hall?
He said to him: A raiding troop came to our city,
and sought to plunder the entire city,
so we slaughtered a calf for them and fed them,
and sent them away in peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשִׁמְעוֹן הַתִּימְנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge from a ברייתא against רב הונא's ruling in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that baking for soldiers can be permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about preparing food for soldiers on יום טוב seems to treat it as improper. The decisive line comes in step 26, and the challenge is spelled out in step 27.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בבא criticizes slaughtering for the soldiers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes. רבי יהודה בן בבא tells שמעון התימני that the town's gain may have been outweighed by its loss, because the תורה permits preparing food on יום טוב only 'for you' and not for גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I wonder whether your gain was not cancelled out by your loss. The תורה said 'for you,' and not for גוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it started in the previous step. It shows how רבי יהודה בן בבא reacted to the townspeople slaughtering a calf for the soldiers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The townspeople avoided trouble with the soldiers, which was their 'gain.' But they may have violated יום טוב, which was their 'loss.' The source for the prohibition is the word לָכֶם in the פסוק about preparing food on יום טוב: cooking is allowed for Jews, not for גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'for you.' The word in the פסוק that limits יום טוב food preparation to Jews

phrases.english: He said to him: I wonder
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי יהודה בן בבא, answering שמעון התימני.

phrases.english: whether your gain was not cancelled out by your loss,
phrases.notes: You saved yourselves from the soldiers, but you lost by breaking יום טוב.

phrases.english: for the Torah said:
'for you,' and not for gentiles.
phrases.notes: From the פסוק: 'only what is eaten by every soul may be done for you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: תָּמֵהַּ אֲנִי אִם לֹא יָצָא שְׂכַרְכֶם בְּהֶפְסֵדְכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 25 by giving its ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not slaughter or cook on יום טוב for גוים, because the Torah says לָכֶם, 'for you.'

steps.title: But the calf could have been eaten by Jews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the slaughter was forbidden, since Jews could have eaten from the calf. By רב הונא's logic, that should have made it allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why was it forbidden? The calf was fit for eating from it!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the ברייתא into a challenge against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא allowed baking for the soldiers when every loaf could also go to a Jew. Here too, a Jew could have eaten from the calf. Yet the ברייתא still treats the slaughter as forbidden, which seems to contradict רב הונא.

phrases.english: But why?
phrases.notes: Why did רבי יהודה בן בבא consider it forbidden?

phrases.english: It was fit to eat from it!
phrases.notes: A Jew could have eaten some of the calf.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? הָא חֲזֵי לְמֵיכַל מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling of the ברייתא to challenge רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling (step 24) that cooking for soldiers is allowed when the food is also fit for a Jew.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The calf was also fit for Jews, yet the ברייתא forbids slaughtering it. So 'fit for a Jew' does not seem to be enough, contrary to רב הונא.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The calf was a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the calf was a טרפה. No Jew could eat it, so it was slaughtered only for the גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It was a טרפה calf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends רב הונא by explaining the case differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the calf was a טרפה, no Jew could eat it at all. So the slaughter was purely for the גוים, which לָכֶם forbids. This matches רב הונא: he forbids cooking whenever the food is not fit for a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal with a fatal defect, forbidden for a Jew to eat

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It was a treifah calf.
phrases.notes: A Jew could not eat it, so it was only for the soldiers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: עֵגֶל טְרֵפָה הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the calf was a טרפה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the calf was kosher and fit for Jews, which would contradict רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The calf was a טרפה, unfit for any Jew, so slaughtering it was only for גוים and forbidden. רב הונא stands.

steps.title: But a טרפה is still fit for dogs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that even a טרפה calf can feed dogs, so it could count as slaughtered for the Jews' dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was fit for dogs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if no Jew could eat the טרפה, Jews' dogs could. If cooking for animals is allowed on יום טוב, the calf was still 'fit' for a permitted use. Then the slaughter should not have been forbidden.

phrases.english: But it was fit for dogs!
phrases.notes: A טרפה may be fed to dogs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא חֲזֵי לִכְלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's answer from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's answer that the calf was a טרפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טרפה is still food for dogs. If feeding animals counts as לָכֶם, the slaughter had a permitted purpose and should have been allowed.

steps.title: Cooking for animals is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that whether one may prepare food for animals on יום טוב is a dispute between תנאים. The ברייתא follows the view that it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the dog question in a single phrase, then moves to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some תנאים hold that animals are not included in לָכֶם. According to them, being fit for dogs does not help, and the ברייתא follows that view.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to one side of a dispute of תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone allows preparing food for animals on יום טוב, so a טרפה fed to dogs should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some תנאים forbid preparing food for animals on יום טוב. The ברייתא of שמעון התימני follows them.

steps.title: The ברייתא: does 'every soul' include animals?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that 'every soul' might include animals, since animals are called נפש elsewhere. Then the word לָכֶם comes to teach otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'Only what is eaten by every soul may be done for you.' From 'every soul' I would think even an animal's soul is included, as it says 'one who strikes the soul of an animal shall pay for it.' Therefore the פסוק says 'for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves there is a dispute of תנאים about cooking for animals. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase לְכׇל נֶפֶשׁ ('every soul') could include animals, since the Torah calls an animal a נפש in the laws of damages. The extra word לָכֶם limits it: food preparation is for people, not animals. That is the opinion that fits the ברייתא of the calf.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the matter is closed. The ברייתא continues past this point, and the other תנא's view, which includes animals, comes next.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'Only that which is eaten'

phrases.aramaic: לְכׇל נֶפֶשׁ הוּא לְבַדּוֹ יֵעָשֶׂה לָכֶם״,
phrases.english: 'by every soul, that alone may be done for you,'
from the implication of what is said, 'every soul,'

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אֲפִילּוּ נֶפֶשׁ בְּהֵמָה בַּמַּשְׁמָע,
phrases.english: I would understand that even an animal's soul is implied,
as in the matter that is stated:
'And one who strikes the soul of an animal shall pay for it,'
phrases.notes: Vayikra 24:18. An animal is called a נפש.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says 'for you.'
phrases.notes: This limits it to people, not animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״אַךְ אֲשֶׁר יֵאָכֵל לְכׇל נֶפֶשׁ הוּא לְבַדּוֹ יֵעָשֶׂה לָכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source showing the dispute of תנאים claimed in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that some תנאים forbid preparing food for animals on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading לָכֶם as excluding animals, even though 'every soul' might have included them.
